Laser printers are consistently more reliable than inkjet printers, based on Consumer Reports' surveys.

Consumer Reports' surveys, based on 69,886 individual printers purchased between 2016 and 2024, indicate significant differences in reliability among printer brands and types, particularly for inkjet printers.

Many inkjet printers are designed for the lowest possible selling price, often leading to lower long-term reliability due to complex internal machinery (motors, pulleys, gears) that can fail. [Consumer Reports]
Initial savings on inexpensive inkjet printers are often offset several times over by high ink costs during the first few years of ownership. [Consumer Reports]
Consumer Reports rarely recommends traditional inkjet printers due to their hidden costs and reliability problems, which lead to low owner satisfaction ratings.
Solid alternatives to traditional inkjets include laser printers and tank-style inkjets. [Consumer Reports]
Inkjet printers are suitable if you don't print a lot and need a combination of text, graphics, and photos (especially in color), but be aware of their drawbacks. [Consumer Reports]

report.summary: For most homes in 2026, a monochrome Brother laser is the most reliable, cheapest-to-run choice. If you need color, the Brother MFC-L3780CDW color laser and Canon G3270 MegaTank ink tank are the strongest all-in-one picks, with the HP M209d as the ultra-budget laser and Epson models covering high-volume ink and photo needs.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Monochrome Laser All-In-One
pros: Wirecutter hands-on testing [Apr 28, 2026] names it best for home use — reliable, cheap to buy and run, simple to operate
Laser reliability advantage confirmed by Consumer Reports surveys of 69,886 printers — laser consistently more reliable than inkjet
Brother ranked most reliable brand per Consumer Reports via BGR [Feb 22, 2026]
All-in-one with print/scan/copy vs single-function competitors
cons: Monochrome only — not suitable if you need color graphics or photos, where Consumer Reports says inkjet is better
Higher upfront cost than cheapest cartridge inkjets under $100, though lower long-term cost
One Brother model in PCMag testing was stymied by slow print speeds, showing speed varies by model
products.verdict: The safest default for most homes. Wirecutter hands-on testing confirms reliability and low running cost, and Consumer Reports survey data backs laser over inkjet for longevity. If you rarely need color, this is the one to buy.
products.best_for: most home users who print documents and need scan/copy
